questions.q: Why do churn-model monitors usually combine input drift checks with outcome metrics?
options: Outcome metrics are cheaper to compute than PSI
Drift checks are more accurate than AUC
Labels arrive late, so drift checks give an early warning while outcome metrics confirm harm later
Outcome metrics are only needed during training
questions.explain: Input checks need no labels and fire immediately. Outcome metrics such as AUC only become available once true outcomes are known.

questions.q: In the lesson's alert rules, how is the critical AUC floor chosen?
options: Always exactly 0.5
The training baseline AUC minus a tolerance (0.744 - 0.05 = 0.694)
Twice the PSI limit
The AUC from the previous week
questions.explain: Thresholds are anchored to the baseline measured at validation time, with a tolerance for normal weekly noise.

questions.q: In week 8 of the simulation, mean predicted probability is 0.118 while the actual cancel rate is 0.065. What does that indicate?
options: The model is well calibrated
The model's probabilities no longer match reality, a calibration gap
The input data has no drift
PSI has been computed incorrectly
questions.explain: Calibration means predicted rates match actual rates. A gap of about 0.05 means the probabilities overstate the true cancel rate.

questions.q: Week 5's AUC of 0.688 sits just under the 0.694 floor, but its bootstrap interval is roughly 0.64 to 0.72. What is the best alert design?
options: Page immediately on any single breach
Disable AUC alerts entirely
Lower the floor to 0.5
Require consecutive breaches before paging, so noise does not trigger alerts
questions.explain: One week of about 165 positives is noisy. Requiring two consecutive breaches reduces false alarms and alert fatigue.

questions.q: Which routing follows the lesson's advice?
options: Warnings to a dashboard or channel, critical alerts to a person
Every alert to a person's phone
Every alert to email only
Critical alerts to a dashboard, warnings to a person
questions.explain: Reserve paging for problems that need action now, otherwise people learn to ignore alerts.
